# Parallax

Header: `winui/ui/scrolling/Parallax.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/scrolling/Parallax.hpp`.

Moves its single child at a different rate than another element scrolls, typically a background image behind a list or scroll view.

The child is laid out larger than the view by the shift, clipped to the view, and moved every frame through its own translation, which the [Parallax](#uiparallax) controls from then on. The source is any element with [`Element::scroll_info()`](../tree/element.md#scroll_info), such as a [`Scroll`](scroll.md#uiscroll) or a [`ListView`](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview). The [Parallax](#uiparallax) does not own it and notices when it is destroyed. Set it after the tree is built. A source destroyed first stops the parallax. A [Parallax](#uiparallax) is never focusable. [`ui::Parallax`](#uiparallax) is the declarative form. It has no [`.source`](#source) field, so set the source through `.control`.

Example: 
```cpp
auto row = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);

auto* parallax = row->add(std::make_unique<ui::ParallaxControl>());
parallax->set_vertical_shift(300.0f); // the background travels 300 DIPs over the whole scroll
parallax->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Background"));

auto* scroll  = row->add(std::make_unique<ui::ScrollControl>());
auto  content = std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Tall content");
content->set_min_height(2000.0f);
scroll->set_child(std::move(content));

parallax->set_source(scroll); // non-owning; both already live in the same tree
window.set_content(std::move(row));
```

## `ui::Parallax`

Moves one child at a different rate than another element scrolls. Builds a [ui::ParallaxControl](#uiparallaxcontrol). There is no `.source` field. Call `set_source()` on [`.control`](#uiparallax-control) once both the view and its source exist.

Example: 
```cpp
const std::vector<std::string>         titles{"Arches", "Bryce Canyon", "Zion"};
ui::Control<ui::Parallax>              parallax;
ui::Control<ui::ListView<std::string>> list;

window.set_content(ui::Grid{
    .height  = 700.0f,
    .content = {
        ui::Cell{.content = ui::Parallax{.vertical_shift     = 500.0f,
                                         .vertical_alignment = ui::Alignment::Leading,
                                         .control            = parallax,
                                         .content            = ui::Image{.source = ui::Bitmap::read("cliff.jpg")}}},
        ui::Cell{.content = ui::ListView<std::string>{.items = titles, .control = list}},
    },
});
parallax->set_source(list); // follow the list's scrolling
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Parallax{
    .horizontal_shift, .vertical_shift, .horizontal_source_start_offset,
    .horizontal_source_end_offset, .vertical_source_start_offset, .vertical_source_end_offset,
    .horizontal_source_offset_kind, .vertical_source_offset_kind, .max_horizontal_shift_ratio,
    .max_vertical_shift_ratio, .horizontal_shift_clamped, .vertical_shift_clamped, .style,
    .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height,
    .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

| <span id="uiparallax-vertical_shift_clamped"></span>`vertical_shift_clamped` | `bool` | `true` | As [`horizontal_shift_clamped`](#uiparallax-horizontal_shift_clamped). |

## `ui::ParallaxControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

Moves its single child at a different rate than another element scrolls, typically a background image behind a list or scroll view.

The child is laid out larger than the view by the shift, clipped to the view, and moved every frame through its own translation, which the [Parallax](#uiparallax) controls from then on. The source is any element with [`Element::scroll_info()`](../tree/element.md#scroll_info), such as a [`Scroll`](scroll.md#uiscroll) or a [`ListView`](../controls/list-view.md#uilistview). The [Parallax](#uiparallax) does not own it and notices when it is destroyed. Set it after the tree is built. A source destroyed first stops the parallax. A [Parallax](#uiparallax) is never focusable. [`ui::Parallax`](#uiparallax) is the declarative form. It has no [`.source`](#source) field, so set the source through `.control`.

Example: 
```cpp
auto row = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);

auto* parallax = row->add(std::make_unique<ui::ParallaxControl>());
parallax->set_vertical_shift(300.0f); // the background travels 300 DIPs over the whole scroll
parallax->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Background"));

auto* scroll  = row->add(std::make_unique<ui::ScrollControl>());
auto  content = std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Tall content");
content->set_min_height(2000.0f);
scroll->set_child(std::move(content));

parallax->set_source(scroll); // non-owning; both already live in the same tree
window.set_content(std::move(row));
```

### ParallaxControl

```cpp
ParallaxControl() = default
```

An empty view with no child, no source and zero shift on both axes.

### set_child

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_child(std::unique_ptr<T> child)
```

Takes ownership of the moving content and returns a non-owning pointer to it. The [Parallax](#uiparallax) controls the child's translation from then on.

### child

```cpp
Element* child() const
```

The content set by [`set_child()`](#set_child) (non-owning), or nullptr.

### source

```cpp
Element* source() const
```

The scrolling element to follow ([Element::scroll_info()](../tree/element.md#scroll_info)), or nullptr for none. Becomes nullptr by itself once the source is destroyed.

### set_source

```cpp
void set_source(Element* source)
```

Follows [`source`](#source), which the [Parallax](#uiparallax) does not own. Pass nullptr to stop following. Redraws.

### horizontal_shift

```cpp
float horizontal_shift() const
```

How far the child moves over the source's horizontal range, in DIPs. 0, the default, is no parallax on that axis. The child is laid out this much larger than the view on that axis.

### set_horizontal_shift

```cpp
void set_horizontal_shift(float shift)
```

Lays the view out again, since the child's size depends on the shift, and redraws.

### vertical_shift

```cpp
float vertical_shift() const
```

Vertical counterpart of [`horizontal_shift()`](#horizontal_shift).

### set_vertical_shift

```cpp
void set_vertical_shift(float shift)
```

Lays the view out again and redraws.

### horizontal_source_start_offset

```cpp
float horizontal_source_start_offset() const
```

Where the horizontal parallax starts on the source's scroll range, in DIPs. It is added to the automatic value or used as is, depending on the offset kind. 0 by default, as are the other offsets.

### set_horizontal_source_start_offset

```cpp
void set_horizontal_source_start_offset(float offset)
```

Redraws. The shift is recomputed on the next frame.

### horizontal_source_end_offset

```cpp
float horizontal_source_end_offset() const
```

Where the horizontal parallax ends on the source's scroll range (see the start offset).

### set_horizontal_source_end_offset

```cpp
void set_horizontal_source_end_offset(float offset)
```

Marks the view for redraw.

### children_hit_clip

```cpp

```

The child is clipped to the bounds, and so is where it can be hit.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Measures the child with the shift added to the available size. The [Parallax](#uiparallax) takes the available size, or the child's size on an unbounded axis.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Arranges the child larger than the view by the shift. A child that stretches grows by the same ratio on the other axis.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the child clipped to the view. Its translation carries the shift.

## Enumerations

### ParallaxSourceOffsetKind

```cpp
enum class ParallaxSourceOffsetKind
```

Whether a [Parallax](#uiparallax) source start or end offset is added to the automatic value (Relative, the default) or used as it is (Absolute).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Absolute` | The offset is the scroll position itself, in unzoomed DIPs. |
| `Relative` | The offset is added to the automatically computed start/end. |
